name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 9 points on the partisan baseline
Jacqui Irwin holds a large fundraising and cash-on-hand edge over Sam Gallucci
Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near 95 percent
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 9-point Democratic lean, Irwin's clear money advantage, and markets pricing her near 95 percent all point to a comfortable hold, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with only a modest trim for the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or a top-two runoff matchup that consolidates the electorate differently could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview: Democrats are strongly favored to hold this Ventura County-area seat now that Julia Brownley is retiring. The district leans Democratic by 9 points, and the fundamentals point to a margin near 18 points once the favorable national environment is layered on. Jacqui Irwin has raised more than double what Sam Gallucci has, with about $295,000 on hand to his $34,000, and outside groups have spent on her behalf while none have opposed her. Prediction markets put her chances near 95 percent. The main caveat is that this is an open seat with no public polling, so uncertainty is somewhat elevated, but every available signal points to a Democratic hold in the mid-to-high teens.
